involves finitely many nonzero terms; it therefore defines an object $P_{Z}(\mathbf{k})$ of $\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(Z,\mathbf{k})$ . Theorem 10.4 and Proposition 12.1 imply that $P_{Z}(\mathbf{k})$ represents the functor $\mathsf{F}$ . Since $\mathsf{F}$ is exact, $P_{Z}(\mathbf{k})$ is projective. Since $\mathsf{F}$ is faithful, $P_{Z}(\mathbf{k})$ is a generator of the category $\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(Z,\mathbf{k})$ (see e.g. [Bas, chap. II, §1]).
Specifically, for each object $\mathscr{A}\in\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(Z,\mathbf{k})$ , there exists an epimorphism $P_{Z}(\mathbf{k})^{n}\twoheadrightarrow\mathscr{A}$ for some $n\geq 0$ (because the $\mathbf{k}$ -module $\Hom_{\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(Z,\mathbf{k})}(P_{Z}(\mathbf{k}),\mathscr{A})$ is finitely generated).

12.2 Structure of the projective objects

Let $Y\subset Z$ be closed subsets of $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G}$ , unions of finitely many
${G_{\mathcal{O}}}$ -orbits. Let $i:Y\to Z$ be the inclusion. The functor ${}^{p}i^{*}:={}^{p}\hskip-1.0pt\mathscr{H}^{0}\bigl(i^{*}(\bm{?})\bigr)$ maps $\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(Z,\mathbf{k})$ to $\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(Y,\mathbf{k})$ and is the left
adjoint to the inclusion $i_{*}:\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(Y,\mathbf{k})\to\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(Z,\mathbf{k})$ .

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
